source: https://obliqq.framer.ai/ (public Framer site), observed 2026-10-22 with rea-agents 6.5.0
how_values_were_obtained: Numbers below are Framer effect settings read from the site's exported component modules (REA export_web_scripts output), cross-checked against scenario screenshots. They are parameters, not code. REA's semantic graph does not retain object-literal property values in Framer's minified ESM, so the literal/property traces came back empty (see rea-site-literals.json and traces/).

stack.runtime: Framer site runtime + Framer Motion chunk + React (25 ES modules from framerusercontent.com)
stack.smooth_scroll: Lenis via Framer's Smooth Scroll component
stack.canvas_webgl: none (no CANVAS node in the DOM inventory)

behaviours: every descendant with computed overflow:auto gets data-lenis-prevent so nested scroll areas scroll natively
in-page anchor links are routed through lenis.scrollTo
smooth_scroll.ruko_delta: kit SmoothScroll uses duration 1.1 + quartic-out; matching obliqq means duration 1.0 + expo-out. Add data-lenis-prevent to the call captions, engine timeline and console tables.

hero_text_reveal.ruko_delta: kit WordReveal uses blur 14px, y 0.18em, 1 s tween, 0.07 s gap, 0.15 s delay. The obliqq feel is shorter: overdamped spring 163/40, 10 px blur, 10 px rise, 0.05 s gap.

block_appear_on_scroll.trigger: element 50% in view (some at threshold 0), animate once
block_appear_on_scroll.pattern: fade + rise; later siblings start lower AND later, a cascading fan
block_appear_on_scroll.suggested_ladder: sibling i: y_from = 64 + 16*i px, delay = 0.1*i s (i = 0..4); the exact enter/transition pairing per element is not recoverable from counts alone
block_appear_on_scroll.blur: none on blocks (blur is reserved for the hero words)
block_appear_on_scroll.ruko_delta: kit Reveal uses y 18 + blur 8 + 0.55 s tween at -12% margin. For obliqq parity: drop blur on large blocks, use viewport { once: true, amount: 0.5 }, spring 150/30, and increase y and delay per sibling index.

scroll_linked_transforms.mapping: Framer 'layer in view' transform = scroll progress of the element with offset ['start end', 'end end'], interpolated between two targets and smoothed by a spring
scroll_linked_transforms.motion12_recipe: const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({ target: ref, offset: ['start end', 'end end'] }); const v = useSpring(useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [from, to]), spring)

effects.needs: perspective on parent (about 1200px), transform-origin top center

effects.use: media zoom-out inside clipped rounded frame

nav.switch_trigger: a section after the hero enters the viewport (threshold 0); not a pixel scrollY test
nav.ruko_delta: kit Nav docks at scrollY > 40 with layout animation, which is close. Switching on a hero-end sentinel and adding the 10px blur / 25% white / 15% warm-grey border makes it match.

marquee.edge_fade: mask fade 20-25% of width on each side
marquee.scroll_coupling: each frame, the ticker offset is nudged by the window scroll delta times a factor, eased with a 0.1 lerp, so logos speed up while the page scrolls
marquee.motion12_recipe: useAnimationFrame for base drift + useVelocity(useScroll().scrollY) mapped through useTransform/useSpring to add to the offset; wrap with a modulo

hover_and_press.icon_swap: two icons cross-fade opacity 0<->1 on hover

type_and_colour_tokens.backgrounds: sky-blue to sand vertical gradient behind hero and feature screenshots; soft cloud imagery at hero edges

performance_observed.scripts: 25 modules, ~1.45 MB uncompressed (framer runtime 473 KB, page module 286 KB, motion 151 KB, react 145 KB)
performance_observed.notes: Lenis keeps a permanent rAF loop; scroll transforms are springs per element. Headless Chrome numbers, not a field measurement.
